extract:
Marilyn Manson is the stage name of Brian Hugh Warner, who launched the band of the same name in Fort Lauderdale, Florida in 1989. Originally called Marilyn Manson & the Spooky Kids, the group emerged from South Florida's underground club scene, mixing shock-rock theatrics with industrial abrasion. Each early member adopted a stage name fusing a female sex symbol with a male serial killer, a conceit that established the project's fixation on American celebrity and violence. Warner, a former music journalist, drew formative inspiration from Alice Cooper, KISS, David Bowie, and the industrial provocations of Throbbing Gristle and Ministry, all of which would shape the band's aesthetic trajectory across the next three decades.

The band caught the attention of Trent Reznor, who signed them to his Nothing Records imprint under Interscope and produced their 1994 debut Portrait of an American Family, preceded by the single Get Your Gunn, written in response to the murder of abortion provider David Gunn. The 1995 covers-and-remix EP Smells Like Children, which included the hit reworking of the Eurythmics' Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This), became their commercial breakthrough. Reznor again co-produced 1996's Antichrist Superstar, a bleak concept record recorded in New Orleans that spawned The Beautiful People and pushed the band into platinum sales and mainstream infamy amid protests from religious groups.

Mechanical Animals (1998) pivoted sharply toward glam rock, with Manson adopting the androgynous Omēga persona and channeling Bowie's Ziggy Stardust era on tracks like The Dope Show and I Don't Like the Drugs (But the Drugs Like Me). The live document The Last Tour on Earth followed in 1999. Holy Wood (In the Shadow of the Valley of Death), released in 2000, closed a trilogy begun with Antichrist Superstar and arrived amid intense scrutiny after politicians and pundits blamed the band for the Columbine shootings, a charge Manson answered pointedly in Michael Moore's Bowling for Columbine. The Golden Age of Grotesque (2003), influenced by Weimar cabaret and produced with Tim Skold, debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and yielded This Is the New Shit, followed by a cover of Depeche Mode's Personal Jesus in 2004.

Eat Me, Drink Me (2007) turned inward and gothic, driven by singles Heart-Shaped Glasses (When the Heart Guides the Hand) and Putting Holes in Happiness, and marked a period of collaboration and personal turbulence around Manson's relationships with Dita Von Teese and Evan Rachel Wood. Later albums including The High End of Low, Born Villain, The Pale Emperor, and Heaven Upside Down saw the artist working with collaborators like Tyler Bates and continuing to tour arenas worldwide, while side ventures included acting roles in Sons of Anarchy and Salem and a long-running visual art practice in watercolor.

Critically, Manson has been treated as both a serious provocateur in the lineage of Cooper and Bowie and as a lightning rod for American culture-war anxieties around religion, gun violence, and youth. Since 2021, multiple women, most prominently Evan Rachel Wood, have publicly accused him of sexual assault and abuse, prompting his dismissal from Loma Vista Recordings, dropped television roles, and ongoing civil litigation that has substantially reshaped the reception of his legacy.
title: Marilyn Manson
